requirement_text.REQ-124: MOB-2 (docs/mobile/requirements.md) needs GET /tenant-config to return { realm_url, locales, default_locale, branding, environment_kind } WITHOUT a bearer token: the mobile app calls it to discover which realm to authenticate against, so by definition it has no token yet. Verified against lib/ on 2026-08-21, this is two gaps, not one: (a) Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig is a stub whose routes land in REQ-078; and (b) Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline mounts it behind Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline, so implementing the route is not sufficient -- it would still demand the token the caller cannot have. Resolve (b) explicitly: either an unauthenticated variant mounted ahead of AuthPipeline, or a documented exemption inside it. Pick one and record why in the moduledoc. This is the gate for the entire mobile tier -- without it the app cannot reach a login screen -- which is why it is sequenced first in docs/mobile/build-order.md phase M-0. Security scope: an unauthenticated endpoint returning per-tenant data is a tenant-data path by definition and needs SECURITY-REVIEWER. The response must expose only what bootstrap requires. Check the shape field-by-field against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md -- in particular whether an unauthenticated caller enumerating slugs can learn which tenants exist, and what the answer should be for a slug that does not exist.

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/mobile/tenant-config returns the five specified fields for a known tenant slug with no Authorization header, demonstrated by a test that sends no token
the auth-pipeline placement question is resolved explicitly and the chosen mechanism is stated in the moduledoc with its reason
a test asserts that the endpoint exposes no field beyond the five specified -- an exact-shape assertion, not a subset check
the behaviour for an unknown tenant slug is decided, tested, and justified against tenant-enumeration risk in the moduledoc
every other route under Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline still requires authentication, proven by a test that would fail if the exemption were pipeline-wide

result.summary: Independently re-ran scripts/test_parallel.sh as a blocking foreground call (not the prior report's numbers taken on trust): combined 1765 tests, 5 properties, 3 failures (1767/1770 passed) -- exact match to TEST-RUNNER's rerun1 report. Pulled the 3 failing test names/lines directly from partition 1's own log (not the report's prose): all 3 are test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs (H6 fixture-classification, lines 106/127/297), identical to ISS-0273. Verified the ISS-0273 attribution structurally rather than accepting it: `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base main HEAD)...HEAD` does not include lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex or its test file, confirming the failure is not in this branch's diff; docs/issues/ISS-0273.yaml exists (status: open, github_issue 537) and independently states the same merge-base reproduction (e5cce4794524401e77e7993a2cd3027c03feb8d1) documented in the report. Ran the two REQ-124-owned test files directly as well (mix test test/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config_test.exs test/letflow/identity_test.exs): 46/46 passed, 0 failures. All 5 acceptance criteria re-verified against actual code/tests, not summaries: AC1 PASS -- lib/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config.ex `get "/"` returns the 5-field map via mobile_config_map/1; test/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config_test.exs describe "AC1/AC3" dispatches through Letflow.Router.call/2 with get_req_header(conn, "authorization") == [] asserted before the call. AC2 PASS -- moduledoc section "Why this is mounted on Letflow.Router, NOT in Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline" states the mechanism (forwarded from Letflow.Router, before the /api/v1 forward, same pattern as REQ-078's /api/tenant-config) and the reason (Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline has no public-path bypass, read in full, so mounting behind it would make the route unreachable by its only caller). AC3 PASS -- test asserts `Map.keys(body) |> Enum.sort() == @expected_keys` (sorted-key-set equality against the literal 5-key list), an exact-shape assertion, not a subset/pattern match; confirmed present in 3 separate test cases. AC4 PASS -- moduledoc "Anti-enumeration" section states the decision (every miss/nil-realm/lookup-error/missing-slug path falls through to the byte-identical default body) and justifies it against enumeration risk; describe "AC4" test asserts 4 distinct inputs (missing slug, unknown slug, nil-realm slug, empty-string slug) produce byte-identical response bodies. AC5 PASS -- test "GET /api/v1/tenants with no Authorization header still returns 401" dispatches through the same Letflow.Router and asserts 401, which would fail if the AC124 exemption had leaked pipeline-wide; lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex confirmed unchanged (still `plug(Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline)` ahead of :match/:dispatch, no new forwards added by this branch's diff). Checked docs/requirements.yaml (REQ-124 entry: status in_progress, as expected pre-DOC-UPDATER) and docs/status/requirement_status.v3.yaml (only a 'started' event recorded for REQ-124, no 'done' yet) -- neither is stale; both correctly reflect that Step 6/DOC-UPDATER has not run yet. No decision-record contradictions found; Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig (REQ-078) is confirmed untouched in behavior and now shares Letflow.Identity.safe_get_tenant_by_slug/2 with the new module (hoisted per the Step 2a rework), consistent with both modules' moduledocs.
